Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Reference inventory and camera reasoning:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps, and
uncertain or occluded regions. These estimates must come from the current input.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only emitted parts; it does not establish image completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.

Record a compact set of image landmarks distributed across the frame and apparent depth.
Include structural line directions, near and far silhouettes, visible border intersections,
and recognizable endpoints where available. Distinguish an object that is actually cropped
in the photograph from one that should remain visible. Do not assume the image center is
the horizon or the camera target. Estimate horizon and convergence from multiple consistent
line families when available; mark ambiguous evidence uncertain. Do not force a symmetric
layout or centered view when the image supports asymmetry.

Choose a consistent arbitrary world scale. Keep camera position, target, lens, shift and
major scene dimensions explicit. Reason about camera height and orientation together with
field of view and scene depth. Aiming at a chosen world point couples pitch to camera and
target heights and horizontal separation. Focal length changes field of view; it does not
independently correct viewing direction. Camera translation also changes parallax. These
parameters can compensate for one another in a single view, so prefer the simplest plausible
configuration consistent with several independent image constraints.

Before expanding repeated objects and fine detail, mentally project the main scene masses
and the landmark set through the proposed camera. Check that near and far objects occupy
plausible image regions and that visible border objects are not accidentally excluded.
Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving the second available for correction;
do not spend an execution on an incomplete calibration scene. Repeated groups may share
construction parameters, but their count, spacing and variation must follow visible evidence.
Do not impose a uniform grid merely because it is easy to generate.

For composite objects, match silhouette and the distribution of occupied space and gaps
before adding fine repeated details. Estimate component sizes relative to their parent and
nearby objects. A correct outer bounding box alone does not ensure correct internal density,
component proportions or visible coverage. Keep these parameters explicit and editable.

Rendered review and correction:
After a successful render, compare the reference inventory against the full rendered view:
missing or extra visible parts, border clipping, silhouette, gaps, relative sizes, overlaps,
structural line directions and image bounds. Review near and far regions and both sides of
the frame. Approximate projected bounding boxes are supporting evidence; they do not measure
visible silhouettes or account fully for occlusion. Inspect the image as well.

Identify the largest supported discrepancies before revising. If several independent landmarks
share a coherent projection error, consider a camera correction. If most landmarks match and
one region differs, consider local position, depth, dimensions or orientation. Neither pattern
proves a unique cause. A border mismatch alone is insufficient reason to move the whole camera.
Check whether candidate camera changes would disrupt already matching regions. Conversely,
do not distort many independent assets to compensate for one plausible shared camera error.

For the available correction, choose a small coherent parameter change with an explicit
qualitative prediction for both mismatching and matching landmarks. Avoid simultaneously
changing camera, unrelated geometry and materials without separate evidence. If a camera
revision is supported, resolve that shared projection discrepancy before interpreting residual
local placement errors. Retain matching objects, semantic groups and support relationships.
Record the intended correction and remaining uncertainty briefly in program comments.
After execution, check the predicted visual effects when a rendering and review budget exist.
An unexecuted revision or an unreviewed render is not verified improvement.

Treat material appearance, exposure, illumination, texture frequency and rendering grain as
separate possible contributors to image mismatch. Do not infer a geometric cause from grain
or a scalar image score. Do not change runner rendering settings to address noise. Procedural
surface detail should have plausible projected scale and contrast, without hiding geometry
errors. Prioritize large image structures before adding surface detail.

Use actual supplied execution decisions and observations as evidence, with their limitations.
Do not manufacture probe outcomes or translate a selected diagnostic module into a fixed
parameter update. A scalar improvement under one perturbation is local sensitivity evidence,
not proof of a unique cause or of improvement under another change. An isolated-object view
can clarify emitted membership and silhouette; its full-image score does not justify removing
the rest of the scene. Missing observations leave competing explanations unresolved.
Functional passes establish mechanical or declared-part integrity only. Unknown semantic
completeness and support/collision truth remain unknown. Surface crossings can include
intentional joints and are not automatically defects. Preserve explicit failures and unknowns.

Execution cost planning:
The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. Use the
runtime's remaining budget to decide whether another build is possible. A short Python loop
can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists. Plan a compact complete
first build so realization and the runner's render can finish with time for review. Do not
change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade this budget.

Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. Each ball, rod and box emits a separate mesh and marker; a fillet_box
can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits 2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and
layout helpers duplicate their contents. Boolean operands also incur mesh creation and
modifier work. Count these expansions, not just named assets.
Aim initially for a few hundred primitive meshes across the whole scene, as a planning
heuristic rather than a measured runtime guarantee or fixed object count. Allocate detail
according to visible pixel size, silhouette and gaps. If the estimate reaches thousands,
simplify repeated microstructure before execution while retaining inventory objects and
meaningful editable parts. Represent unresolved surface detail with shared materials and
restrained procedural shading; retain geometry that changes contours, openings or occlusions.
Avoid nested per-element decoration below image resolution. Use short, adaptively spaced
tube paths, concentrating points at bends. Avoid many nearly identical Boolean slices to
approximate one hollow shape; use a small number of appropriate solids and cutters.
Prefer boxes or scaled balls where their silhouettes suffice; reserve fillet_box for parts
whose rounded edges matter. Reuse a small material palette for each surface family rather
than generating distinct random colors and materials for tiny primitives. Keep parent assets,
semantic child parts and support relations intact during simplification.
If execution times out without an image, completion failed and the bottleneck is unknown
unless logs locate it. When a retry remains, reduce expanded primitive counts, Boolean work
and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera, coverage or appearance
defects from a timeout. A reduced-cost build still needs execution and rendered verification.

Execution verification:
realize(scene) clears Blender to an empty factory scene. Configure the world, camera,
lighting and materials after realization; do not assume a default world exists. When setting
world nodes, use this initialization after realize:
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.world is None:
        sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('SceneWorld')
    sc.world.use_nodes = True
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background')
    if background is None:
        background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')
    if output is None:
        output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
and fillet radii against the smallest dimension. If execution fails, use the actual traceback
to repair the program. A failed execution without an image supplies no rendered visual
feedback: do not treat it as evidence for unrelated camera or geometry changes. Do not
claim verification when no successful render exists.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
import random

# Reference inventory, normalized image bounds:
# Room: cream walls and ceiling, mustard lower wall band, tan tiled floor.
# Left openings .00-.31/.15-.58; right doors/windows .72-1/.12-.65.
# Raised stage .37-.66/.24-.46, dark red curtain, green side curtains,
# scalloped cream valance and a freestanding green chalkboard.
# Wooden desks/benches fill .00-.94/.42-.89 with substantial open leg gaps.
# Foreground left desk .14-.36/.59-.89, central desk .50-.71/.56-.82,
# right desk .76-.93/.53-.73. Bags below and beside several desks.
# Ceiling fans at .06-.26/.00-.09, .64-.87/.00-.09, and smaller fans deeper.
# Black wall speakers, portraits, fluorescent fixtures and exposed ceiling beams.
# Backstage detail and objects behind desks remain uncertain.
#
# Landmarks: floor/wall borders converge near (.51,.39); left yellow band
# runs from (0,.42) to (.36,.43), right band from (1,.46) to (.65,.40).
# Stage upper edge spans (.38,.24)-(.66,.24); board (.47,.33)-(.58,.42).
# Foreground left table corners approximately (.14,.61),(.35,.60),(.35,.67).
# Ceiling back intersection at y=.22; near fans are genuinely top-cropped.
# Camera horizon approximately .40, uncertain due to desk occlusions.
#
# Scale: meters. Room width 8.6, depth 15.6, height 4.5.
# Camera (0,-2,1.85), lens 25 mm; downward pitch about 5 degrees.
# Primitive estimate: architecture/openings ~125, 22 desk assemblies ~242,
# bags ~35, stage ~35, fans/lights/pictures ~80: approximately 520 meshes.
# No boolean work, fillet expansions, or dense repeated microstructure.

random.seed(8)
scene = Scene("Classroom")
cream = (.84, .83, .66)
white = (.94, .94, .85)
yellow = (.91, .69, .015)
wood = (.29, .22, .115)
edge = (.37, .30, .17)
topwood = (.27, .245, .17)
dark = (.035, .042, .034)
metal = (.22, .22, .18)

def cube(parent, name, size, center, color):
    obj = box(size=size, center=center, color=color)
    parent.include(name, obj)
    return obj

def beam(parent, name, a, b, r, color):
    obj = rod(radius=r, start=a, end=b, color=color)
    parent.include(name, obj)
    return obj

room = Asset("Architecture")
scene.include("Architecture", room)
cube(room, "Tiled_floor", (8.7,18,.12), (0,7,.0), (.64,.52,.32))
cube(room, "Left_cream_wall", (.15,16,4.5), (-4.37,7.8,2.25), cream)
cube(room, "Right_cream_wall", (.15,16,4.5), (4.37,7.8,2.25), cream)
cube(room, "Rear_wall", (8.7,.18,4.5), (0,15.7,2.25), cream)
cube(room, "Left_yellow_band", (.035,16,1.05), (-4.278,7.8,.55), yellow)
cube(room, "Right_yellow_band", (.035,16,1.05), (4.278,7.8,.55), yellow)
cube(room, "Rear_yellow_band", (8.6,.035,1.05), (0,15.58,.55), yellow)
cube(room, "Ceiling", (8.8,17,.15), (0,7.5,4.57), white)
for i,y in enumerate([2.2,7.1,11.8]):
    cube(room, "Ceiling_cross_beam_%d"%i, (8.6,.24,.26), (0,y,4.37), white)
for x in [-2.25,2.25]:
    cube(room, "Ceiling_long_beam_%s"%x, (.19,16,.16), (x,7.7,4.43), white)
for x in [-4.23,4.23]:
    cube(room, "Skirting_%s"%x, (.06,16,.12), (x,7.7,.12), (.43,.36,.19))

# Surface detail uses a single tile shader with restrained stone variation.
# The thin grid represents visible tile joints, without tile mesh proliferation.
def opening(side, y, width, kind, index):
    a = Asset("%s_%s_%02d"%(side,kind,index))
    scene.include(a.name, a)
    x = -4.265 if side == "Left" else 4.265
    sign = 1 if side == "Left" else -1
    if kind == "Window":
        z0, h = 1.30, 2.02
        cube(a,"Bright_glazing",(.027,width,h),(x,y,z0+h/2),(.86,.91,.88))
        # Tall brown window shutters and clear central aperture.
        for d in [-1,1]:
            cube(a,"Side_frame_%d"%d,(.10,.075,h+.18),(x+sign*.055,y+d*width/2,z0+h/2),wood)
            cube(a,"Shutter_%d"%d,(.075,width*.19,h*.87),(x+sign*.10,y+d*width*.39,z0+h*.47),(.32,.22,.105))
        for z in [z0,z0+h,z0+h*.78]:
            cube(a,"Crossbar_%s"%z,(.11,width+.1,.065),(x+sign*.055,y,z),wood)
        cube(a,"Center_mullion",(.09,.045,h),(x+sign*.07,y,z0+h/2),wood)
    else:
        h=2.8
        cube(a,"Door_leaf",(.06,width,h),(x+sign*.05,y,h/2),(.36,.25,.135))
        for d in [-1,1]:
            cube(a,"Door_jamb_%d"%d,(.14,.10,h+.12),(x+sign*.07,y+d*width/2,h/2),(.44,.32,.19))
        cube(a,"Door_header",(.14,width+.16,.12),(x+sign*.07,y,h),edge)
        for k in [-.28,.28]:
            cube(a,"Door_panel_%s"%k,(.025,width*.35,h*.75),(x+sign*.09,y+k*width,h*.48),(.43,.31,.17))
        cube(a,"Door_handle",(.075,.045,.12),(x+sign*.13,y+width*.32,1.25),(.65,.60,.39))

for i,(y,w,k) in enumerate([(1.15,1.35,"Window"),(3.65,1.0,"Door"),
                            (5.7,1.25,"Window"),(8.15,.95,"Door"),
                            (10.4,1.15,"Window"),(12.6,.85,"Door")]):
    opening("Left",y,w,k,i)
for i,(y,w,k) in enumerate([(1.5,1.0,"Door"),(4.3,1.4,"Window"),
                            (7.0,1.05,"Door"),(9.3,1.35,"Window"),
                            (12.1,1.05,"Door")]):
    opening("Right",y,w,k,i)

stage=Asset("Stage")
scene.include("Stage",stage)
cube(stage,"Platform",(5.35,2.05,.3),(-.05,14.45,.20),(.43,.32,.16))
cube(stage,"Dark_backdrop",(4.8,.10,2.65),(-.05,15.35,1.86),(.075,.026,.019))
cube(stage,"Proscenium_top",(5.5,.18,.20),(-.05,13.82,3.47),white)
for x in [-2.66,2.59]:
    cube(stage,"Green_side_curtain_%s"%x,(.43,.30,2.75),(x,14.03,2.03),(.075,.20,.07))
    cube(stage,"White_outer_pillar_%s"%x,(.13,.28,3.05),(x+(-.29 if x<0 else .29),13.9,1.72),white)
for i in range(11):
    x=-2.36+i*.46
    cube(stage,"Valance_panel_%02d"%i,(.47,.10,.31),(x,13.75,3.28),(.87,.84,.66))
    scallop=ball(radius=.235,center=(x,13.75,3.16),color=(.87,.84,.66))
    scallop.resize((1,.25,.55))
    stage.include("Valance_scallop_%02d"%i,scallop)
for i in range(7):
    cube(stage,"Curtain_fold_%d"%i,(.12,.10,2.2),(-1.95+i*.62,15.25,1.8),(.12,.045,.025))

board=Asset("Freestanding_chalkboard")
scene.include("Freestanding_chalkboard",board)
cube(board,"Green_writing_face",(2.05,.065,.98),(.12,13.15,1.43),(.095,.25,.18))
for x in [-.94,1.18]:
    cube(board,"Frame_vertical_%s"%x,(.055,.09,1.07),(x,13.11,1.43),(.39,.38,.28))
    beam(board,"Stand_%s"%x,(x,13.13,.27),(x,13.13,1.97),.024,metal)
    beam(board,"Foot_%s"%x,(x,12.83,.25),(x,13.55,.25),.025,metal)
for z in [.91,1.95]:
    cube(board,"Frame_horizontal_%s"%z,(2.17,.09,.055),(.12,13.11,z),(.42,.42,.30))
beam(board,"Diagonal_chalk_line",(-.72,13.07,1.04),(-.41,13.07,1.83),.008,(.65,.71,.59))
cube(stage,"Blue_side_notice",(.55,.08,1.27),(2.05,13.95,1.25),(.28,.65,.77))

def desk(name,x,y,w=1.65):
    a=Asset(name)
    scene.include(name,a)
    cube(a,"Desktop",(w,.63,.09),(x,y,.89),topwood)
    cube(a,"Front_apron",(w-.06,.065,.18),(x,y+.235,.75),edge)
    cube(a,"Book_shelf",(w-.15,.43,.055),(x,y,.59),(.27,.22,.13))
    for dx in [-w/2+.08,w/2-.08]:
        for dy in [-.23,.23]:
            cube(a,"Desk_leg_%s_%s"%(dx,dy),(.065,.065,.84),(x+dx,y+dy,.44),edge)
    # The paired bench sits behind its desktop, visible as a narrow horizontal strip.
    cube(a,"Bench_seat",(w-.08,.29,.075),(x,y+.75,.49),(.31,.26,.15))
    for dx in [-w/2+.15,w/2-.15]:
        cube(a,"Bench_leg_%s"%dx,(.07,.18,.46),(x+dx,y+.75,.24),edge)
    cube(a,"Bench_stretcher",(w-.25,.055,.065),(x,y+.75,.21),edge)
    return a

# Rows are offset and vary in width as in the photograph.
placements=[
(-1.85,2.35,1.75),(-3.9,3.8,1.45),
(.95,4.2,1.85),(3.13,5.3,1.65),
(-2.12,5.35,1.65),(-3.65,6.4,1.4),
(.92,6.55,1.7),(2.85,7.7,1.5),
(-2.05,7.45,1.62),(-.25,8.4,1.52),
(.94,8.8,1.68),(-2.0,9.25,1.6),
(2.9,9.6,1.45),(.98,10.45,1.6),
(-1.95,10.8,1.55),(-.25,11.5,1.4),
(2.85,11.4,1.4),(.95,12.0,1.5),
(-1.9,12.15,1.5),(-3.7,8.8,1.3),
(-3.6,11.0,1.25),(3.15,12.65,1.25)]
for i,(x,y,w) in enumerate(placements):
    desk("Pupil_desk_%02d"%i,x,y,w)

def bag(name,x,y,z,color,scale=1):
    a=Asset(name)
    scene.include(name,a)
    body=ball(radius=1,center=(x,y,z+.29*scale),color=color)
    body.resize((.22*scale,.145*scale,.35*scale))
    a.include("Fabric_body",body)
    pocket=ball(radius=1,center=(x,y-.125*scale,z+.22*scale),color=tuple(c*.82 for c in color))
    pocket.resize((.17*scale,.065*scale,.19*scale))
    a.include("Front_pocket",pocket)
    beam(a,"Zipper",(x-.12*scale,y-.18*scale,z+.35*scale),
         (x+.12*scale,y-.18*scale,z+.35*scale),.009*scale,(.46,.53,.48))
    beam(a,"Handle_left",(x-.07*scale,y,z+.59*scale),(x-.055*scale,y,z+.71*scale),.018*scale,dark)
    beam(a,"Handle_right",(x-.055*scale,y,z+.71*scale),(x+.065*scale,y,z+.60*scale),.018*scale,dark)
    beam(a,"Loose_strap",(x+.14*scale,y+.04,z+.48*scale),
         (x+.30*scale,y-.02,z+.035),.018*scale,dark)

bag("Foreground_black_backpack",-2.75,1.75,.08,(.018,.035,.055),1.1)

bag("Left_blue_bag",-2.85,6.0,.46,(.02,.28,.60),.7)

# Flat black satchel beneath foreground desk.
satchel=Asset("Satchel_under_left_desk")
scene.include("Satchel_under_left_desk",satchel)
cube(satchel,"Soft_case",(.66,.26,.14),(-1.65,2.3,.21),(.018,.023,.021))

# Small visible schoolbooks and papers on selected desktops.
props=Asset("Desktop_objects")
scene.include("Desktop_objects",props)
for i,(x,y) in enumerate([(-2.15,5.35),(-3.7,6.4),(.88,4.2),
                            (-1.9,9.25),(2.9,9.6),(-.25,11.5)]):

    if i%2==0:
        cube(props,"Book_cover_%d"%i,(.36,.24,.012),(x,y,.975),(.32,.13,.19))

def fan(name,x,y,z,r):

    scene.include(name,a)

    hub.resize((1,1,.55))
    a.include("Motor_hub",hub)
    for k in range(3):
        ang=math.radians(18+120*k)
        cx=x+math.cos(ang)*r*.54
        cy=y+math.sin(ang)*r*.54
        blade=box(size=(r*.95,.16*r,.025),center=(cx,cy,z),color=(.25,.235,.20))
        blade.turn('z',math.degrees(ang))
        a.include("Blade_%d"%k,blade)
for i,(x,y,z,r) in enumerate([(-2.2,1.8,4.03,.87),(2.1,2.2,4.08,.90),
                              (-1.85,8.0,4.01,.63),(1.9,8.4,4.03,.62),
                              (0,13.0,4.02,.46)]):
